> **What this case shows** — the [partial-correlation sibling](../sway-cognition-partial-bds/index.qmd)
> found the sway–cognition link is mostly age; its open question asked for a fuller multivariable model.
> Here it is. The **newly-authored** `multipleRegression` fits sway ~ age + Trail Making Test A,
> reproducing base R **`lm`** **bit-for-bit** and **`statsmodels`** OLS to machine precision. In the joint
> model **age dominates** (β=1.59 cm/year, p=2e-8) while **cognitive speed adds nothing** (β=0.12, p=0.55).
> The model explains ~28% of sway variance — essentially all of it from age.

::: {.callout-tip title="The recipe you'll learn"}
**Workflow** — a response + predictors matrix → `multipleRegression()` → read the coefficient table and fit.
**Way of thinking** — a partial correlation answers "does this one association survive?"; a multiple
regression answers the whole question at once — each predictor's independent contribution and how much the
model explains. Put the candidate predictors in together and let the coefficients adjudicate.
**Ecosystem usage** — `PhysioMoCap::swayMetrics()`, `PhysioAnalysis::multipleRegression()`.
:::

## Proposition

In the multiple OLS regression of eyes-closed-foam sway on age and TMT-A (n=158), age is significant
(β=1.59, p=2e-8) and TMT-A is not (β=0.12, p=0.55); the model R²=0.276, F(2,155)=29.5, p=1.4e-11;
`multipleRegression` reproduces base R `lm` bit-for-bit and `statsmodels` OLS to machine precision.

## Question & goal

**The question is the complete multivariable decomposition: with age and cognition in the model together,
what independently predicts sway?** The partial-correlation sibling certified that the cognitive effect
largely vanishes under age adjustment and deferred the full model; this fold fits it, authoring the
multiple-regression op.

## Challenge & approach

We take each subject's eyes-closed-foam sway (from `swayMetrics`, certified against the Prieto reference in
the [sway-posturography-bds](../sway-posturography-bds/index.qmd) case), age and TMT-A, and fit
`multipleRegression` — checking every coefficient, the R² and the F against base R `lm` and `statsmodels`.

```
158 subjects: sway ~ age + TMT-A   (OLS, via QR)
  age:    beta = 1.59 cm/year   (p = 2e-8)   <- dominant
  TMT-A:  beta = 0.12 cm/s       (p = 0.55)   <- not significant once age is in
  model:  R2 = 0.276,  F(2,155) = 29.5,  p = 1.4e-11
     vs base R lm         → coefficients |diff| = 0 (bit-for-bit)
     vs statsmodels OLS   → coefficients |diff| ~ 1e-13 (machine precision)
```

## Data

**Santos & Duarte (2016) BDS balance dataset (figshare)**: per subject, eyes-closed-foam COP path length,
age and Trail Making Test A time, for the 158 subjects with all three. Details in
[`artifacts/data_sources.json`](artifacts/data_sources.json).

## Results

![Left: the coefficient forest plot — age (red) sits well away from zero with a tight interval (p=2e-8), while TMT-A (grey) straddles zero (p=0.55). Right: −log10(p) for the two predictors — age towers over the significance line, TMT-A falls below it. The model (R²=0.28, F(2,155)=29.5) is essentially all age.](artifacts/figure.png)

*How to read this:* with both predictors in the model, only age's coefficient is distinguishable from zero.
TMT-A's marginal correlation with sway (certified earlier) is fully absorbed by age — its adjusted
contribution is indistinguishable from nothing.

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| **age coefficient** | **1.59 cm/year** (p = 2e-8) |
| **TMT-A coefficient** | **0.12** (p = 0.55, ns) |
| model **R²** / adj R² | **0.276** / 0.267 |
| F (df 2, 155) | 29.5 (p = 1.4e-11) |
| n | 158 |
| vs base R `lm` (\|diff\|) | **0** (bit-for-bit) |
| vs `statsmodels` OLS (\|diff\|) | **< 1e-9** (~1e-13) |

The coefficients equal base R exactly and statsmodels to machine precision. Values trace to
[`artifacts/mlr_summary.csv`](artifacts/mlr_summary.csv).

## Conclusion

`multipleRegression` reproduces the reference on the certified `swayMetrics`. The transferable takeaway:
**put the competing predictors in one model and read the coefficients. Here it closes the cognitive-motor
thread cleanly — the marginal link between cognitive speed and sway is entirely age; cognition adds nothing
once age is accounted for. The coefficient t-test on TMT-A reproduces the partial correlation exactly, two
views of the same adjustment.**

## Open questions

- The model is linear and additive; an age × cognition interaction, non-linear age terms, or additional
  predictors (vestibular function, strength, medication) might reveal structure this two-predictor model
  cannot. The complete two-predictor OLS is the honest resolution of the partial-correlation case's call for
  a fuller model. *Documented, not escalated.*

## Using this in your own analysis

| Step | Function | Package |
|---|---|---|
| Posturography sway metrics | `swayMetrics()` | PhysioMoCap |
| Multiple OLS regression | `multipleRegression()` | PhysioAnalysis |
| Simple regression / partial correlation | `linearRegression()`, `partialCorrelation()` | PhysioAnalysis |

**Reading the result.**

- **coefficient + p** — each predictor's effect holding the others fixed; a predictor whose marginal
  association vanishes here was explained by the others.
- **R² and F** — how much the whole model explains and whether it beats nothing; report them alongside the
  coefficients.

**The recipe, copy-runnable:**

```r
library(PhysioAnalysis)

# first column = response, remaining columns = predictors
multipleRegression(cbind(sway, age, tmt))   # coefficient table + R2/F -- bit-for-bit vs base R lm
```

**Auditing the numbers.** Every value on this page traces to
[`artifacts/mlr_summary.csv`](artifacts/mlr_summary.csv), and [`audit.py`](audit.py) re-checks the
coefficients and p-values, the R² and F, the bit-exact match against base R lm and the machine-precision
match against statsmodels, the age-dominant / TMT-non-significant split, the sample size, and the honestly
noted scope (authors the new multipleRegression op; sway from the certified swayMetrics; cognition fully
accounted for by age; cross-sectional association, additive model).
